open_points.subject: M10 MigrationClosure identity decision
open_points.text: Until 2026-11-11 it was declared a value; the owner's decision of 2026-10-31 that it is a record of its own, addressed by the pointers and the audit, is what SPEC_STANDARD §15.1.1 calls an entity.
open_points.question: How can this be reconciled with the Status statement that on 2026-10-31 “the proposals under M01, M04 and M10 are accepted as written,” when M10 was then declared a value: did the owner accept value identity, accept only the record-of-its-own facts, or decide entity identity?
options: The owner accepted value identity on 2026-10-31 and changed it to entity on 2026-11-11.
The owner decided record-of-its-own/entity identity on 2026-10-31, but State 1 classified it incorrectly until 2026-11-11.
Only M10's facts and persistence proposal were accepted on 2026-10-31; its identity remained undecided until 2026-11-11.
open_points.default_guess: Treat the 2026-10-31 decision as accepting a record of its own and the 2026-11-11 change as correcting its classification to entity.

open_points.subject: M10 MigrationClosure identity derivation
open_points.text: It is identified by the digest of the file the import accepted, the one identity it has (codex round-04 T1); Registry mints no identifier for it.
open_points.question: Who produces the digest that becomes the entity's identity, and from which authoritative representation of the accepted file: Registry from the received bytes, the external migration script, or the owner as import input?
options: Registry computes the digest from the exact bytes it accepts.
The migration script supplies the digest and Registry stores it.
The owner supplies the digest with the import.
The file contains its own asserted digest.
open_points.default_guess: Registry computes the digest from the exact accepted file bytes.

open_points.subject: M10 MigrationClosure identity across store histories
open_points.text: Durable, a record of its own, at most one per store (R0-89): an instance that restores a store from before the import may import again, and that store then holds its own closure.
open_points.question: If a pre-import backup is restored and the same file is successfully imported again, is the new closure the same entity because its sole identity is the same digest, or a distinct entity scoped to the new store history?
options: The digest is globally sufficient, so both closures are the same entity.
Identity is scoped by store history, so equal digests can identify distinct closures.
Identity is scoped by the physical store or instance rather than its history.
open_points.default_guess: Scope the identity by store history, making the two closures distinct entities despite equal digests.

witness.initial: A backup exists from before any import in a store; the migration file F has digest D.
events: The owner successfully imports F, and Registry records closure C1 identified by D.
The live store is lost, and the owner restores the pre-import backup outside Registry.
The owner successfully imports the same file F again, and Registry records closure C2 identified by D.
outcomes: Because the digest is the one identity, C1 and C2 are the same entity.
Because each restored store history holds its own closure, C1 and C2 are distinct entities.
witness.observer: The owner or a recovery/audit tool comparing the two store histories and their closure references.

open_points.subject: M12 AuditSequence continuity on restore
open_points.text: A restored store holds this record as the backup holds it, the same record continued; Registry neither knows nor records that the store was restored.
open_points.question: When a backup with an older sequence number replaces a later lost store, is the carried AuditSequence the same entity whose value has gone backward, or a new store-history entity initialized from the backup; and what action is considered to create that entity if Registry creates one only with a new empty store?
options: It is the same entity, and restore may lower it outside Registry's guarantees.
It is a distinct AuditSequence entity for the new store history, initialized by the external restore.
It is the same entity, but changes lost after the backup are deemed never to have belonged to its history.
open_points.default_guess: Treat the restored history as having a distinct AuditSequence entity initialized from the backup snapshot, while preserving its stored number.

witness.initial: A checked backup contains AuditSequence 5; afterward the live store appends entries through sequence 9.
events: The owner replaces it with the backup outside Registry.
Registry starts on the restored store and appends the next audit entry.
outcomes: The same AuditSequence entity continues from 9 at the historical level but is now stored as 5, contradicting “never lowered.”
A new store-history AuditSequence begins from the copied value 5 and advances to 6, contradicting “the same record continued” and requiring an unlisted creation event.
witness.observer: The owner comparing pre-loss and restored audit records, or an implementation deciding entity continuity and the next append.
